heading: Cold open
narration: A hydrothermal vent is an opening in the seafloor where seawater that has soaked down into hot rock flows back out, heated and loaded with dissolved minerals.

heading: Cold open
narration: NOAA puts the hottest of that fluid at up to 400 degrees Celsius, and deep-ocean pressure keeps it liquid.

heading: Cold open
narration: The evidence comes from instruments sent down by submersibles, fluid samples missing their magnesium, and a 1977 dive that found animals nobody expected.

heading: Cold open
narration: Together they settle the heat and the chemistry. They do not settle how many vents exist.

narration: What is a hydrothermal vent?

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: Vents were expected before they were found. By the time of the first expedition, the theory of seafloor spreading held that new ocean crust forms along mid-ocean ridges, where tectonic plates pull apart and molten rock rises close to the seafloor.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: If that was right, cold ocean water should be seeping into the young, cracked rock, warming up, and escaping somewhere.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: Instruments towed above the Galápagos Rift had recorded faint pulses of warmer water.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: So in 1977, scientists dove in the submersible Alvin, operated by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, to find the source.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: They found the warm springs. Around them they also found something the expedition had not been designed to study: dense clusters of clams, mussels and tube worms, thriving in the dark.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: The team was made up mostly of geologists and geochemists, and the biology arrived as a surprise.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: Two years later, in 1979, Alvin dives on the East Pacific Rise found something hotter.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: Tall mineral chimneys were pouring out what looked like thick black smoke.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: The temperature probe the team carried was not built for it; by WHOI's account, part of it melted.

heading: Geologists predicted vents before anyone saw one
narration: Those first black smokers turned a predicted phenomenon into one of the most closely studied features of the deep ocean.

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Here is the sequence as geochemists reconstruct it. First, cold seawater seeps down through cracks in the crust near a ridge.

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Deeper in, that water is heated by magma sitting below the seafloor.

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Hot water under pressure is chemically aggressive. As it moves through rock it gives up some of its own dissolved ingredients and dissolves metals and sulfide in their place: iron, copper, zinc, and hydrogen sulfide among them.

args.title: How vent fluid forms
args.note: much of what it carries precipitates

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Hot fluid is buoyant, so it rises and exits through the seafloor, often along the same fractures that let it in.

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: When that fluid meets bottom water just above freezing, much of what it carries precipitates almost instantly.

args.boundary: not smoke in any burning sense

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: That is what the black smoke is. NOAA describes it as a cloud of mineral particles, mostly metal sulfides, not smoke in any burning sense.

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Some of those particles settle around the opening, and layer by layer they build a hollow chimney.

args.boundary: not smoke in any burning sense

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Chimneys grow, crack, topple and regrow. Where hot fluid has already mixed with seawater underground, the vent runs cooler, carries lighter-colored minerals, and is called a white smoker.

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Other vents build no chimney at all. They appear only as shimmering water rising from cracks, called diffuse flow.

args.meaning: a vent chimney releasing a cloud of metal sulfide particles
args.boundary: not smoke in any burning sense

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: No one has watched seawater travel down through the crust, so that leg of the loop is inferred.

args.title: Inferring the hidden plumbing
args.conclusion: the water reacted with hot rock

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: The strongest evidence is chemical. Vent fluid collected by submersibles and robotic vehicles comes up almost stripped of magnesium, an element seawater normally carries in abundance.

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: The simplest explanation is that the water reacted with hot rock along the way and left its magnesium behind in new minerals.

args.title: Inferring the hidden plumbing
args.conclusion: the water reacted with hot rock

heading: A vent is the exit of plumbing you cannot see
narration: Seismic surveys that image magma beneath ridges, and laboratory experiments that heat seawater with crushed basalt, point to the same loop.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: At sea level, pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. That is not a property of water alone.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: It is a property of water under the weight of one atmosphere of air.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: On the deep seafloor, the whole ocean above presses down, and the pressure there is many times higher than at the surface.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: The boiling point is set by pressure, and it climbs with it.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: That is why fluid near 400 degrees can leave a chimney as a liquid rather than as a burst of steam.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: Pressure raises the bar, but it does not remove it. Under some combinations of temperature and depth, vent fluid does boil underground, or separates into a lighter, vapor-like phase and a dense, salty brine.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: Scientists detect this after the fact, in the saltiness of what comes out.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: Some vents release fluid fresher than seawater and others release fluid saltier than seawater, and that difference is a fingerprint of separation happening somewhere below.

heading: The water stays liquid because pressure moves the boiling point
narration: At the hottest and deepest extremes, the distinction between liquid and gas stops being meaningful at all.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Almost every food web you know begins with photosynthesis. Sunlight fades quickly with depth, and at most vents there is none at all.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Life there runs instead on chemosynthesis. Microbes capture energy from chemical reactions, most famously by oxidizing the hydrogen sulfide in vent fluid, and use that energy to build sugars from carbon dioxide.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Some live free in the water or on rock. Others live inside animals.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Either way, these microbes are the base of the vent food web.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: The giant tube worm, Riftia pachyptila, shows how far that partnership can go.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Adults have no mouth and no gut. Their red plume, colored by hemoglobin, takes up oxygen, carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide from the surrounding water.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: The blood carries those to an organ called the trophosome, packed with symbiotic bacteria that run the chemistry and feed the worm from within.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: The animal itself lives inside a tough white tube anchored to the rock.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Biologists did not take that arrangement on trust. Several lines of evidence agree.

args.title: How we know the worm is fed by bacteria
args.conclusion: the worm is fed by its symbionts

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Dissection showed there is no mouth and no gut. Microscopy showed bacteria inside the trophosome, densely packed in its cells.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Enzyme measurements found the chemical machinery for fixing carbon using energy from sulfide.

args.title: How we know the worm is fed by bacteria
args.conclusion: the worm is fed by its symbionts

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: And carbon signatures in the worm's tissue match carbon fixed by those bacteria, not carbon from food sinking down from the surface.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Any one of these could be questioned on its own. Together, they show the worm is fed by its symbionts.

args.title: How we know the worm is fed by bacteria
args.conclusion: the worm is fed by its symbionts

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Vent communities also differ from ocean to ocean. Giant tube worms dominate many Pacific sites.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: On the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, swarming shrimp crowd the chimneys instead. In the Indian Ocean, the scaly-foot snail grows a shell layered with iron sulfide.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: Biologists explain these differences partly by how larvae disperse between vent fields that can be far apart, and partly by local chemistry.

heading: Vent life runs on chemistry, not sunlight
narration: How exactly animals colonize a newly formed vent remains an active question.

heading: Some vents run on rock chemistry instead of magma
narration: Black smokers are not the whole story. In 2000, researchers exploring near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge came upon a field of pale, towering chimneys that became known as Lost City.

heading: Some vents run on rock chemistry instead of magma
narration: NOAA Ocean Exploration has documented the site with remotely operated vehicles. Its chimneys are made of carbonate minerals, not metal sulfides, and its fluid is far cooler than a black smoker's and strongly alkaline rather than acidic.

heading: Some vents run on rock chemistry instead of magma
narration: The heat source is different too. Lost City sits on mantle rock that has been pushed up close to the seafloor.

heading: Some vents run on rock chemistry instead of magma
narration: When seawater reacts with that rock, in a process called serpentinization, the reaction itself releases heat, along with hydrogen and methane.

heading: Some vents run on rock chemistry instead of magma
narration: So Lost City is driven by rock chemistry, not driven by magma.

heading: Some vents run on rock chemistry instead of magma
narration: That matters because it means vents can exist away from active volcanic centers, and it gives microbes a different menu of chemical energy to live on.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: Vents also affect the ocean as a whole. Seawater is thought to circulate through hydrothermal systems over very long timescales, and in the process vents add some elements to the ocean and remove others.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: Plumes of dissolved iron from vents have been traced far from their source.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: The minerals left behind form deposits rich in copper, zinc and other metals, which is why vents interest economic geologists as well as biologists.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: Much of this work is published by public bodies: NOAA reports on vent temperatures and expeditions, WHOI on Alvin and the 1977 dives, and the Smithsonian on deep-sea life.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: Vents also sit at the center of one of science's open questions.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: Some researchers propose that life on Earth began at hydrothermal vents, where chemical energy and mineral surfaces were both available, and alkaline systems like Lost City feature heavily in that argument.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: Others favor shallow pools on land, where repeated drying and wetting can concentrate molecules.

heading: Vents shape more than the animals living on them
narration: Laboratory experiments support pieces of both ideas. Neither has been demonstrated, and you should treat any confident claim either way as ahead of the evidence.

heading: Producer POV
narration: Space is fascinating, but Earth bothers me more. We're already here and still don't understand huge parts of it.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: As you watch vent footage, remember that every image is lit by the vehicle itself.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: Without its lamps the scene would be black, so the colors you see are the colors of artificial light on rock and tissue.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: The black smoke looks slow and soft, but it is fluid hot enough to damage instruments not built for it.

heading: What to notice in the edit
narration: Watch, too, for the shimmer above the cooler cracks. That ripple is diffuse flow, warm water bending the light as it rises, and many vent animals live in that milder water rather than in the hottest jets.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: This evidence firmly establishes some things. First, vent fluid stays liquid under pressure, which follows from basic physics and is confirmed by direct measurement.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Second, tube worms are fed by symbionts, shown by several independent lines of evidence.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Other things remain open. No one knows precisely how many vents exist.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: The mid-ocean ridge system is enormous, only a small fraction has been surveyed closely, and estimates vary widely.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: Vents can switch on and off as eruptions and earthquakes reshape the plumbing, so any map is a snapshot.

heading: Evidence limit
narration: And where life began is not settled by anything in this video.

heading: Closing
narration: A hydrothermal vent is seawater returning from a journey through hot rock, carrying the crust's chemistry back into the ocean.

heading: Closing
narration: We know its temperature because instruments were sent into it, its plumbing because of what is missing from its water, and its life because biologists took that life apart and looked.

heading: Closing
narration: Much of the seafloor where such vents could exist has still never been seen.
